terms.meaning: The language that controls how web pages look.
A named value, such as a color, that is reused in many places.
A device setting that asks apps to limit animations for users who find motion uncomfortable.
A styling toolkit that provides short class names for common styles.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Imports and color names
sections.what: Loads the fonts and the shared style files, and maps the app's named colors onto the theme variables. These names are what screens use in their class names.
sections.why: Gives every screen one set of color names that follow the theme.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a color here breaks any screen that uses the old name.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Status colors and shadows
sections.what: Sets the status colors used for green, amber, and red badges, the chart colors, the sidebar colors, the font names, and the soft shadow sizes.
sections.why: Status colors are kept in one place so badges look consistent.
sections.watch_out: The same status colors are copied into the JavaScript color file, so both must change together.

sections.name: :root  (part 1)
sections.title: Base theme values
sections.what: Sets the warm off-white, ink, and line colors, the shadow overlays, and the editorial font, along with the sidebar and button tones.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are the default light-theme values that the dark theme overrides.
sections.watch_out: The dark theme file overrides these values, so a change here may not show in dark mode.

sections.name: :root  (part 2)
sections.title: Base page styles and card styles
sections.what: Applies the base font, background, and heading style to all pages. Also defines the frosted panel, the card style, and the fallback for browsers without blur support.
sections.why: Keeps every page and card on the same look. The fallback keeps panels readable on older browsers.
sections.watch_out: The page background layers depend on the topology motif values, which are set to none in the base theme.

sections.name: :root  (part 3)
sections.title: Small label style and fade-in keyframes
sections.what: Defines the small monospace label style used for metadata and the fade-up animation keyframes.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are reusable styling pieces.

sections.name: .animate-fade-up
sections.title: Fade-up animation class
sections.what: Gives an element a short fade-and-rise animation when it appears.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It adds a gentle entrance effect.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
sections.title: Reduced motion for general styles
sections.what: When the user asks for less motion, turns off page animations, transitions, and smooth scrolling.
sections.why: The comment says the app should honor reduced motion everywhere.
sections.watch_out: Uses an important override, so any new animation must follow this same rule or it will be ignored here.

sections.name: .house-pulse-ring::after
sections.title: Report and house-tool animations
sections.what: Defines the pulsing ring, the shimmer text, and the scanning bar used by the Reality Scan and Lessons Learnt tools, along with their colors.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These give the house tools their progress and thinking effects.
sections.watch_out: Several animations run forever, so they add ongoing motion until the tool stops.

sections.name: .house-shimmer-text
sections.title: Shimmer text and scan bar
sections.what: Gives heading text a moving highlight and sets a scanning bar to sweep back and forth.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It signals that work is in progress.
sections.watch_out: Text highlighting with a clip effect may not render the same in every browser.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
sections.title: Reduced motion for house tools
sections.what: Turns off the house-tool animations when the user asks for less motion, and shows the shimmer text in plain color.
sections.why: Reduced motion must also apply to the house-tool effects, which are not covered by the general rule.
sections.watch_out: A new house-tool animation must be added here too, or it will still move for these users.

summary: The main stylesheet that sets the app's colors, fonts, shadows, spacing names, and animations.
purpose: Defines the visual theme so every screen uses the same look.
why: Colors and shadows are written once here so screens do not invent their own. Motion is limited for users who ask for less movement.
how: First it imports fonts and shared style files. Then it defines named colors and shadows as variables, sets the base page styles, adds reusable card and label styles, and defines the animations. Finally it turns animations off when the user has reduced motion turned on.
inputs: The imported style files, the font service, and the variables set by the theme files.
outputs: Styles applied across the whole app.
risks: Changing a color variable changes every screen that uses it. Some colors are copied into the JavaScript color file and must be kept in step by hand.
debug: If a color looks wrong, search for the variable name here and in the theme files. If an animation plays when it should not, check the reduced-motion block at the end.
